7.text: UBS analyst Erika Najarian favors large-cap banks with excess capital, while Goldman Sachs’ Q3 equities revenues jumped 72% year over year to $6.44 billion. The articles otherwise discuss broad bank earnings expectations, bearing on JPMorgan only as sector context.

4.text: Jamie Dimon warned that AI agents accessing bank accounts pose security risks and named five economic threats: deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising rates, and geopolitics. JPMorgan posted a strong quarter, landed back-to-back trillion-dollar IPO roles for SpaceX and Anthropic, and faces criticism that its AI agent restrictions protect bank profits.

8.text: JPMorgan partnered with Kurtosys on client reporting, backed GT Metabolic's Series C, launched two tokenized money market funds on Solana, and won Anthropic's IPO retail mandate. It also lost a seven-member Houston team to Rockefeller, announced a veteran CEOcircle cohort, and had KBRA rate its 2026-9 mortgage trust.

13.text: JPMorgan holds nearly $900 million in tokenized funds on Ethereum and Solana, and its asset management arm forecasts Bitcoin will return 10% annually over the next decade, beating stocks, bonds, and gold, though it won't recommend buying it.

12.text: JPMorgan's return on tangible common equity hit 24% for the first nine months of FY26, with a CET1 ratio of 13.9%. Analysts also compared it favorably to Goldman Sachs and Bank of America, citing a 29.9% operating margin and 3.3% revenue growth.

5.text: JPMorgan raised price targets on Embraer, Hexagon, Rumo, Bel Fuse, and SpaceX, and called AstraZeneca a compelling risk-reward play. It downgraded Norwegian Cruise Line and Telefonica (on Virgin Media O2 debt risk), and said French political risk leaves sentiment overly bearish.

14.text: JPMorgan brought real-world assets onto Ethereum and joined DTCC's tokenization push alongside BlackRock and Ripple Prime. Otherwise, the articles compare crypto valuations, ETF flows, and price declines across Solana, Ethereum, XRP, Sui, and Bitcoin.
